scholarships.title: Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship Program
scholarships.official_source: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs (administered by the Institute of International Education)

existing.description: The Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship Program is a program of the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs that provides up to $5,000 in merit-based scholarships to outstanding American undergraduate students with high financial need to pursue credit-bearing academic studies and career-oriented internships abroad. It is congressionally funded, established by the U.S. Congress in 2001, and administered by the Institute of International Education since its inception. Applicants must be receiving a Federal Pell Grant during the time of application or be able to prove they will receive one during their term abroad. The programme has funded American students to study and intern abroad in more than 170 countries, with recipients from all 50 U.S. states and D.C.
eligibility: Be receiving a Federal Pell Grant at the time of application, or be able to provide proof that a Pell Grant will be received during the term of the study abroad program or internship
Apply for the correct scholarship term matching the student's programme dates
existing.eligibility_summary: American undergraduate students with high financial need who are receiving, or can prove they will receive, a Federal Pell Grant, and who are enrolled in an eligible credit-bearing study abroad or international internship programme.
benefits: Up to USD 5,000 merit-based scholarship for study abroad or an international internship
Access to the Gilman alumni network of more than 50,000 American students and professionals
coverage: Merit-based scholarship of up to USD 5,000 toward a credit-bearing study abroad programme or career-oriented international internship
requirements: Advisor certification of the submitted application
Submission in Pacific Time; late applications are not accepted
Application for the correct scholarship term according to programme dates
documents: Completed online application in the Gilman portal
Certification of the application by a Study Abroad and Financial Aid advisor at the home institution
Proof of Federal Pell Grant eligibility
Application essays as specified for the cycle
application_method: Submit an online application during the published cycle window
Have a Study Abroad and Financial Aid advisor certify the submitted application before the advisor certification deadline
Await screening by the Gilman Program, recommendation by selection panelists, and review and approval by the U.S. Department of State
existing.selection_notes: Applications move through a published process: the cycle opens, students submit, advisors certify, the Gilman Program screens eligibility, selection panelists recommend eligible applications, the U.S. Department of State reviews and approves, and the Gilman Program sends award notifications to all applicants. 72% of Gilman scholars come from small towns or rural communities.
existing.best_fit: U.S. undergraduates with demonstrated high financial need who hold or will hold Federal Pell Grant eligibility and want credit-bearing study abroad or an international internship aligned with career skills, foreign languages, or national security priorities.
existing.notes: Limited supplemental funding exists through the STEM Supplemental Award for STEM-related coursework or internships abroad and the Critical Need Language Award for languages deemed important to national security. A separate Gilman Skills for America Scholarship provides up to $5,000 for community and technical college students with no additional application essay or minimum programme length requirement, applied for through the general application process.
existing.application_period: Rolling annual cycles by study-abroad term. The application cycle opens mid-January 2027 for the Spring 2027 term; all applicants are notified of their status by email in May 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Fall 2026 application cycle: deadline October 1, 2026 at 11:59PM PT, now closed. Next cycle, Spring 2027: student deadline February 25, 2027 at 11:59pm Pacific Time, with the advisor certification deadline March 4, 2027 and the application cycle opening mid-January 2027.
existing.program_type: Merit-based scholarship for U.S. undergraduates to study or intern abroad

scholarships.title: Phi Kappa Phi Fellowship
scholarships.official_source: The Honor Society of Phi Kappa Phi

existing.funding_period: per fellowship award, in three tiers
existing.description: The Honor Society of Phi Kappa Phi awards 40 Fellowships of $8,500 each, six at $15,000 each, and two at $35,000 each to members entering the first year of graduate or professional study. Established in 1932, the Fellowship Program annually provides funding to first-year graduate students pursuing post-baccalaureate degrees across all academic disciplines. Each active chapter may select one candidate from among its local applicants to compete for the Society-wide awards, and endorsed Phi Kappa Phi Fellows go on to study at some of the nation's top graduate schools. The 2027 cycle opens its application portal on December 15, 2026 and closes at the national deadline of April 15, 2027.
eligibility: Must be an active (dues paid) member through April 15, 2027, or have accepted the invitation to join and be initiated by June 30, 2027
Seeking full-time enrollment status in a graduate/professional school program to begin between May 1, 2027, and February 1, 2028
Have not completed more than 9 hours of semester credits of graduate study in any field at the application deadline
Not be a sitting Phi Kappa Phi board member, divisional vice president, member of the Fellowship Award committee or Society employee at the time of application
Be endorsed by and apply through a local active Phi Kappa Phi chapter, which selects one nominee for the Society-wide competition
existing.eligibility_summary: Active dues-paid Phi Kappa Phi members through April 15, 2027, or who have accepted an invitation to join and will be initiated by June 30, 2027, seeking full-time enrolment in a graduate or professional programme starting between May 1, 2027 and February 1, 2028, with no more than 9 hours of completed graduate semester credits at the application deadline.
coverage: Cash fellowship award toward first-year graduate or professional study
requirements: Active dues-paid membership through April 15, 2027, or accepted invitation with initiation by June 30, 2027
No more than 9 hours of graduate semester credits completed at the application deadline; applicants who completed 10 or more graduate credits on or before April 15 are not eligible
Full-time enrolment in a graduate or professional programme beginning between May 1, 2027 and February 1, 2028
Endorsement and submission through the local chapter by the chapter's own deadline
documents: Completed online application, saved as a PDF
application_method: Complete the application online in the portal, which opens December 15, 2026, and save the completed PDF
Submit the application, official transcripts, work sample and two letters of recommendation to your local chapter by their deadline
Confirm your chapter's preferred means of submission and find your chapter president's email in the online Chapter Directory
Wait for the chapter to select one applicant as its nominee for the Society-wide competition
existing.selection_notes: Selection is based on the applicant's promise of success in graduate or professional study, as evidenced by academic achievement including transcripts, honors and awards, relevant research experience and samples of creative work; service and leadership experience on and off campus; letters of recommendation; a personal statement and career goals; a work sample; and acceptance or application to an approved graduate or professional program.
existing.best_fit: Phi Kappa Phi members entering the first year of a full-time graduate or professional programme anywhere in the U.S. who can route their application through an active local chapter before the chapter deadline.
existing.notes: Each active Phi Kappa Phi chapter may select one candidate from among its local applicants to compete for the Society-wide awards, so chapter access is effectively a prerequisite. The Fellowship Program was established in 1932 and has annually provided funding to first-year graduate students across all academic disciplines.
existing.application_period: Annual cycle. The online application portal opens December 15, 2026; applicants submit to their local chapter in late March or early April 2027; the national deadline is April 15, 2027; recipients are notified in summer 2027.
existing.deadline_display: April 15, 2027: National deadline. The application portal opens December 15, 2026, and applicants must apply through their local chapter by the chapter deadline, which varies but is typically two weeks prior to the national deadline. Recipients are notified in summer 2027.
existing.program_type: Fellowship award for first-year graduate and professional students
